newsitem.title: USA: No additional charges to be filed by prosecutors.
newsitem.headline: No additional charges to be filed by prosecutors.

text.p: The criminal investigation into oil and gas partnerships sold by Prudential Securities Inc. has ended without additional criminal charges being filed, officials said Wednesday.
Prudential agreed in 1994 to pay $330 million in to a special fund for investors after a criminal complaint charged the company with securities fraud relating to the marketing of the partnerships.
The investigation could be reopened if new evidence of criminal wrongdoing by individuals comes to light, U.S. Attorney Mary Jo White said in a statement.
In late 1993, federal prosecutors began the investigation into allegations of fraud in connection with Prudential's marketing of limited partnership interests in the Energy Income Fund.
Under the settlement, Prudential admitted wrongdoing and agreed to the appointment of an outside counsel to insure Prudential's compliance under the settlement agreement.
The monitor and federal prosecutors will continue to watch Prudential until October 1997.
